page_title: Making Movie Monad by David Lettier

summary.title: Making Movie Monad by David Lettier
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build an Electron desktop video player whose HTML, CSS, and JavaScript are generated from Haskell using Blaze, Clay, and Fay.
takeaways: Set up a Haskell project with Stack, a .cabal file, and a makefile that builds HTML, CSS, and JavaScript from Haskell source.
Generate an HTML page with Blaze-html and style it with Clay, a Haskell CSS preprocessor.
Write client-side logic in Haskell with Fay, using fay-jquery and FFI calls to browser APIs such as FileReader.
Run and package the app with Electron and electron-packager, and understand why the file size limit exists (whole file is loaded into memory).
summary.summary: The page is a project-based tutorial that builds "Movie Monad," a desktop video player on Electron. It walks through installing Stack, NVM, Electron and make, then creating the project directory, stack.yaml, movieMonad.cabal, package.json and a makefile. Each source file is explained in turn: Blaze-html generates the page markup, Clay generates the CSS, and Fay compiles Haskell into the browser-side JavaScript that reads a selected file as a data URL and loads it into a video element. Full source for each module is included at the end of each section.
